tagline: AI meeting notepad that turns transcripts into structured notes.
verdictSummary: Recording audio, transcribing it locally with Whisper, and asking an LLM to structure the result into a summary and action items is a genuine one-sitting build — one of the cleanest yes entries in the catalogue. What the paid product mainly adds on top is cross-device sync, a mobile app, and automatic calendar joins.
coreLoopDIY: Record meeting audio, transcribe it with Whisper (locally or via API), send the transcript to an LLM for a structured summary, and save the result as a dated Markdown file.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because it's always on, tied into their calendar and work calls without any setup, and trustworthy enough that meeting history never gets lost.
notes: A poster child for this whole trend: local audio capture, Whisper transcription, and an LLM summary into a Markdown folder is genuinely a one-prompt build.
prompt:
Build a local meeting-notes tool: a simple start/stop recording control that captures system and microphone audio together. On stop, transcribe the recording with whisper.cpp running locally (fully offline, free), or optionally via a hosted Whisper API if a key is present in the environment for faster turnaround. Send the transcript to an LLM (Anthropic or OpenAI, whichever key is configured) with a prompt that returns a short summary, any decisions made, and action items with owners where mentioned. Save the result to a dated Markdown file — summary at the top, full transcript below a divider — with the audio file kept alongside it. Everything stays local except the API calls you explicitly choose to make; with whisper.cpp and a local model, the whole loop can run fully offline.

Do not build cross-device sync, a mobile app, or automatic calendar integration to auto-join meetings — those need infrastructure and platform access well beyond a personal recording tool.

faq.q: Can I import my existing Granola notes?
faq.a: Granola lets you export notes, and since this build also writes plain Markdown files, moving them into the same folder structure is a straightforward copy, not a real migration.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: No — this is a desktop tool tied to capturing your computer's own audio during a call. There's no mobile version and no sync to read notes elsewhere.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Nothing if you stay fully local with whisper.cpp and a local model. Using a hosted Whisper API or a cloud LLM for summaries costs a small amount per meeting, typically well under a dollar.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: Joining meetings automatically. Granola links to your calendar and captures calls without you remembering to hit record; here, forgetting to start the recording means the meeting simply isn't captured.
